topics.title: Represent and solve addition problems with sums between 0 and 10 and subtraction problems using related facts

subtopics.title: Represent and solve addition problems with sums between 0 and 10 and subtraction problems using related facts

outcomes.text: For any number from 1 to 9, use objects to find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number.
Given a number from 0 to 5, find the different ways it can be represented as the sum of two numbers.
Solve addition and subtraction real-world problems within 5 using objects, drawings or equations to represent the problem.
For any number from 1 to 9, find the number that makes 10 when added to the given number.
Given a number from 0 to 10, find the different ways it can be represented as the sum of two numbers.
Solve addition and subtraction real-world problems using objects, drawings or equations to represent the problem.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of the equal sign

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of the equal sign

outcomes.text: Show that an addition or subtraction equation within 5 is true using objects or drawings.
Explain why addition or subtraction equations are true using objects or drawings.

topics.title: Develop an understanding for collecting, representing and comparing data

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding for collecting, representing and comparing data

outcomes.text: Sort objects by characteristic (e.g., size, shape or color). Count the objects in each category and report the results.
Collect and sort objects into categories and compare the categories by counting the objects in each category. Report the results verbally, with a written numeral or with drawings.

topics.title: Identify, compare and compose two- and three-dimensional figures

subtopics.title: Identify, compare and compose two- and three-dimensional figures (1 of 3)

outcomes.text: Identify two- and three-dimensional figures regardless of their size. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.
Sort two-dimensional figures based on their similarities. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles and squares.
Use informal spatial language to describe the relative positions of two-dimensional figures (e.g., above, below, beside, next to, under).
Sort three-dimensional figures based on their similarities. Figures are limited to spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.

subtopics.title: Identify, compare and compose two- and three-dimensional figures (2 of 3)

outcomes.text: Use informal spatial language to describe the relative positions of three-dimensional figures (e.g., above, below, beside, next to, under).
Explore real-world objects that can be modeled by a given two- or three-dimensional figure. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.
Recognize that a different figure can be formed by combining two smaller two-dimensional figures. Figures used to form a composite shape are limited to triangles, rectangles and squares.
Identify two- and three-dimensional figures regardless of their size or orientation. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.

subtopics.title: Identify, compare and compose two- and three-dimensional figures (3 of 3)

outcomes.text: Compare two-dimensional figures based on their similarities, differences and positions. Sort two-dimensional figures based on their similarities and differences. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles and squares.

Compare three-dimensional figures based on their similarities, differences and positions. Sort three-dimensional figures based on their similarities and differences. Figures are limited to spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.
Find real-world objects that can be modeled by a given two- or three-dimensional figure. Figures are limited to circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, spheres, cubes, cones and cylinders.
Combine two-dimensional figures to form a given composite figure. Figures used to form a composite shape are limited to triangles, rectangles and squares.

topics.title: Identify and compare measurable attributes of objects

subtopics.title: Identify and compare measurable attributes of objects

outcomes.text: 1a. Explore the attributes of a single object that can be measured such as length or weight.
1b. Directly compare two objects to determine which is longer/shorter or heavier/lighter.
1c. Express the length of an object, up to 10 units long, as a whole number of lengths using non-standard objects laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps.
Identify the attributes of a single object that can be measured such as length, volume or weight.
Directly compare two objects that have an attribute which can be measured in common. Express the comparison using language to describe the difference.
Express the length of an object, up to 20 units long, as a whole number of lengths by laying non-standard objects end to end with no gaps or overlaps.

topics.title: Develop an understanding for counting using objects in a set

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding for counting using objects in a set (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Given a group of up to 10 objects, count the number of objects in that group and represent the number by identifying the written numeral. Express the number of objects in a rearrangement of that group without recounting.
Given a number from 0 to 10, count out that many objects.
Identify the first, second or third object within a sequence.
Compare the number of objects from 0 to 10 in two groups to determine which group is greater or less, or if the number of objects in the two groups are equal.

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding for counting using objects in a set (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Given a group of up to 20 objects, count the number of objects in that group and represent the number of objects with a written numeral. State the number of objects in a rearrangement of that group without recounting.
Given a number from 0 to 20, count out that many objects.
Identify positions of objects within a sequence using the words “first,” “second,” “third,” “fourth” or “fifth.”
Compare the number of objects from 0 to 20 in two groups using the terms less than, equal to or greater than.

topics.title: Recite number names sequentially within 100 and develop an understanding for place value

subtopics.title: Recite number names sequentially within 100 and develop an understanding for place value

outcomes.text: Express number names from 1 to 100 by ones and from 10 to 100 by tens. Starting at a given number, count forward to 20 and backwards within 10.
Represent whole numbers from 10 to 19, using one group of 10 ones and some further ones, with objects, drawings or verbalization.
Locate and compare two numbers from 0 to 10 to determine which number is less than, equal to or greater than the other number.
Recite the number names to 100 by ones and by tens. Starting at a given number, count forward within 100 and backward within 20.
Represent whole numbers from 10 to 20, using a unit of ten and a group of ones, with objects, drawings and expressions or equations.
Locate, order and compare numbers from 0 to 20 using the number line and terms less than, equal to or greater than.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of addition and subtraction operations with one-digit whole numbers

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of addition and subtraction operations with one-digit whole numbers

outcomes.text: Explore addition and subtraction of two whole numbers within 5 using objects.
Apply a strategy for adding and subtracting two one-digit whole numbers to solve within 5.
Explore addition of two whole numbers from 0 to 10, and related subtraction facts.
Add two one-digit whole numbers with sums from 0 to 10 and subtract using related facts with procedural reliability.

topics.title: Solve addition problems with sums between 0 and 20 and subtraction problems using related facts

subtopics.title: Solve addition problems with sums between 0 and 20 and subtraction problems using related facts

outcomes.text: Apply the commutative property of addition to find a sum of two whole numbers within 20.
Solve addition and subtraction real-world problems within 10 using objects, drawings or equations to represent the problem.
Apply properties of addition to find a sum of three or more whole numbers.
Solve addition and subtraction real-world problems using objects, drawings or equations to represent the problem.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of the relationship between addition and subtraction

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of the relationship between addition and subtraction

outcomes.text: Use the relationship between addition and subtraction to explore subtraction as addition with a missing addend
Determine if addition or subtraction equations (with no more than three terms) are true or false. Sums may not exceed 10 and their related subtraction facts.

Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation, relating three whole numbers, with the result unknown (e.g., 8 − 2 = __, __ = 7 + 3). Sums may not exceed 10 and their related subtraction facts.
Restate a subtraction problem as a missing addend problem using the relationship between addition and subtraction.
Determine and explain if equations involving addition or subtraction are true or false.
Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation, relating three whole numbers, with the unknown in any position.

topics.title: Collect, represent and interpret data using pictographs and tally marks

subtopics.title: Collect, represent and interpret data using pictographs and tally marks

outcomes.text: Sort data into two categories and represent the results using tally marks or pictographs.
Interpret data represented with tally marks or pictographs to determine how many in each category and compare the values of two categories of data in terms of more or less.
Collect data into categories and represent the results using tally marks or pictographs.
Interpret data represented with tally marks or pictographs by calculating the total number of data points and comparing the totals of different categories.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of fractions by partitioning shapes into halves and fourths

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of fractions by partitioning shapes into halves and fourths

outcomes.text: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal-sized parts. Recognize the parts of the whole as halves or fourths.
Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal-sized parts. Name the parts of the whole using appropriate language including halves or fourths.

topics.title: Identify and analyze two- and three-dimensional figures based on their defining attributes

subtopics.title: Identify and analyze two- and three-dimensional figures based on their defining attributes (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Sort and identify two- or three-dimensional figures based on their defining attributes. (e.g., number of sides, vertices, edges, faces, etc., rather than color, orientation or size). Figures are limited to circles, semi-circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, trapezoids, hexagons, spheres, cubes, rectangular prisms, cones and cylinders.
Produce two-dimensional figures when given defining attributes. Figures are limited to triangles, rectangles and squares.

Recognize that different figures can be formed by putting together smaller two- or three-dimensional figures and that smaller figures can be formed by taking apart larger two- or three-dimensional figures. Figures are limited to semi-circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, rectangular prisms, cones and cylinders.

Explore real-world objects with parts that can be modeled by a given two- or three-dimensional figure. Figures are limited to semi-circles, triangles, rectangles, squares and hexagons, spheres, cubes, rectangular prisms, cones and cylinders.

subtopics.title: Identify and analyze two- and three-dimensional figures based on their defining attributes (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Identify, compare and sort two- and three-dimensional figures based on their defining attributes. Figures are limited to circles, semi-circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, trapezoids, hexagons, spheres, cubes, rectangular prisms, cones and cylinders.
Sketch two-dimensional figures when given defining attributes. Figures are limited to triangles, rectangles, squares and hexagons.
Compose and decompose two- and three-dimensional figures. Figures are limited to semi-circles, triangles, rectangles, squares, trapezoids, hexagons, cubes, rectangular prisms, cones and cylinders.

Given a real-world object, identify parts that are modeled by two- and three-dimensional figures. Figures are limited to semi-circles, triangles, rectangles, squares and hexagons, spheres, cubes, rectangular prisms, cones and cylinders.

topics.title: Compare and measure the length of objects

subtopics.title: Compare and measure the length of objects

outcomes.text: Use a ruler to measure the length of an object with exact whole units to the nearest inch.
Explore familiar objects that can be used to develop a mental measurement benchmark to understand the relative size of an inch.
Compare and order the length of up to three objects using direct comparison.
Estimate the length of an object to the nearest inch. Measure the length of an object to the nearest inch or centimeter.
Compare and order the length of up to three objects using direct and indirect comparison.

topics.title: Tell time and identify the value of coins and combinations of coins and dollar bills

subtopics.title: Tell time and identify the value of coins and combinations of coins and dollar bills (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Using analog and digital clocks, express the time in hours.
Identify the names and values of pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters.
Find the value of a group of only pennies, only nickels or only dimes up to $1.
Find the value of a group of only one-, only five- or only ten-dollar bills up to $100.

subtopics.title: Tell time and identify the value of coins and combinations of coins and dollar bills (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Using analog and digital clocks, tell and write time in hours and half-hours.
Identify pennies, nickels, dimes and quarters, and express their values using the ¢ symbol. State how many of each coin equal a dollar.
Find the value of combinations of pennies, nickels and dimes up to one dollar, and the value of combinations of one, five and ten dollar bills up to $100. Use the ¢ and $ symbols appropriately.

topics.title: Extend counting sequences and understand the place value of two-digit numbers

subtopics.title: Extend counting sequences and understand the place value of two-digit numbers (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Starting at a given number, count forward within 100 and backwards within 20 by ones. Skip count by 5s from 5 to 100.
Read numbers from 0 to 20 written in standard form and expanded form. Generate numbers from 0 to 20 using standard form.
Compose and decompose numbers up to 20 using tens and ones. Demonstrate each composition or decomposition with objects, drawings, and expressions or equations.
Order (e.g., 5, 9, 13) and compare (e.g., 11 19) whole numbers up to 20.

subtopics.title: Extend counting sequences and understand the place value of two-digit numbers (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Starting at a given number, count forward and backwards within 120 by ones. Skip count by 2s to 20 and by 5s to 100.
Read numbers from 0 to 100 written in standard form, expanded form and word form. Write numbers from 0 to 100 using standard form and expanded form.
Compose and decompose two-digit numbers in multiple ways using tens and ones. Demonstrate each composition or decomposition with objects, drawings and expressions or equations.
Plot, order and compare whole numbers up to 100.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of addition and subtraction operations with one- and two-digit numbers

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of addition and subtraction operations with one- and two-digit numbers (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Recall addition facts with sums to 5 and related subtraction facts.
Apply a strategy for adding and subtracting two one-digit whole numbers to solve within 10.
Identify the number that is one more and one less than a given number within 20.
Explore the addition of a two-digit number from 11 to 19 and a one-digit number.
Explore subtraction of a one-digit number from a two-digit number from 11 to 19.

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of addition and subtraction operations with one- and two-digit numbers (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Recall addition facts with sums to 10 and related subtraction facts with automaticity.
Add two whole numbers with sums from 0 to 20, and subtract using related facts with procedural reliability.
Identify the number that is one more, one less, ten more and ten less than a given two-digit number.
Explore the addition of a two-digit number and a one-digit number with sums to 100.
Explore subtraction of a one-digit number from a two-digit number.

topics.title: Solve addition problems with sums between 0 and 100 and related subtraction problems

subtopics.title: Solve addition problems with sums between 0 and 100 and related subtraction problems

outcomes.text: Solve one-step addition and subtraction real-world problems within 20 using objects.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems.

topics.title: Demonstrate an understanding of equality and addition and subtraction

subtopics.title: Demonstrate an understanding of equality and addition and subtraction

outcomes.text: Determine if addition or subtraction equations with no more than three terms are true or false. Sums may not exceed 20 and their related subtraction facts.

Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation, relating three whole numbers, with the change or result unknown (e.g., 7 + _ = 10, 10 − 3= ?). Sums may not exceed 20 and their related subtraction facts.
Determine and explain whether equations involving addition and subtraction are true or false.
Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation, relating three or four whole numbers, with the unknown in any position.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of multiplication

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of multiplication

outcomes.text: Explore the concept of odd and even by pairing objects to represent an even number using two equal groups or represent an odd number by using two equal groups with one left over. Group of objects may not exceed 20.

Explore using repeated addition to find the total number of objects represented in a collection of equal groups (e.g., 3 groups of 2 objects) or in a rectangular array (e.g., 3 rows of 2 objects). Total objects may not exceed 20.
Represent an even number using two equal groups or two equal addends. Represent an odd number using two equal groups with one left over or two equal addends plus 1.
Use repeated addition to find the total number of objects in a collection of equal groups. Represent the total number of objects using rectangular arrays and equations.

topics.title: Collect, categorize, represent and interpret data using appropriate titles, labels and units

subtopics.title: Collect, categorize, represent and interpret data using appropriate titles, labels and units

outcomes.text: Sort data into up to three categories and represent the results using tally marks, tables, pictographs or bar graphs. Align data with given title, labels and units.

Interpret data represented with tally marks, tables, pictographs or bar graphs to solve one-step put-together and take-apart problems. Pictograph symbols and bar graph intervals may only represent a quantity of 1.
Collect, categorize and represent data using tally marks, tables, pictographs or bar graphs. Use appropriate titles, labels and units.
Interpret data represented with tally marks, tables, pictographs or bar graphs including solving addition and subtraction problems.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of fractions

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of fractions

outcomes.text: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal-sized parts. Recognize the parts of the whole as halves, thirds or fourths. Explore the whole as two halves, three thirds or four fourths.
Partition circles and rectangles into two, three or four equal-sized parts. Name the parts using appropriate language, and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds or four fourths.
Partition rectangles into two, three or four equal-sized parts in two different ways showing that equal-sized parts of the same whole may have different shapes.

topics.title: Identify and analyze two-dimensional figures and identify lines of symmetry

subtopics.title: Identify and analyze two-dimensional figures and identify lines of symmetry

outcomes.text: Identify and produce two-dimensional figures when given defining attributes. Figures are limited to triangles, rectangles, hexagons and squares.
Sort two-dimensional figures based on the number of sides, number of vertices, whether they are closed or open and whether the sides are curved or straight.
Identify a line of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure.
Identify and draw two-dimensional figures based on their defining attributes. Figures are limited to triangles, rectangles, squares, pentagons, hexagons and octagons.
Categorize two-dimensional figures based on the number and length of sides, number of vertices, whether they are closed or not and whether the edges are curved or straight.
Identify line(s) of symmetry for a two-dimensional figure.

topics.title: Describe perimeter and find the perimeter of polygons

subtopics.title: Describe perimeter and find the perimeter of polygons

outcomes.text: Explore perimeter as an attribute of a figure that can be measured by placing unit segments along the boundary without gaps or overlaps. Find perimeters of rectangles by counting unit segments.
Find the perimeter of a polygon with whole-number side lengths given. Polygons are limited to triangles, rectangles and squares.
Explore perimeter as an attribute of a figure by placing unit segments along the boundary without gaps or overlaps. Find perimeters of rectangles by counting unit segments.
Find the perimeter of a polygon with whole-number side lengths. Polygons are limited to triangles, rectangles, squares and pentagons.

topics.title: Measure the length of objects and solve problems involving length

subtopics.title: Measure the length of objects and solve problems involving length (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Measure the length of an object to the nearest inch, foot and or yard when given the appropriate tool.
Explore estimation strategies by developing measurement benchmarks of familiar objects that could be used to make reasonable estimates of length to the nearest inch, foot, or yard.
Measure the lengths of two objects using the same unit (i.e., inch, foot, yard) and determine the difference between their measurements.
Solve one-step real-world measurement problems involving addition and subtraction of lengths within 20 given in the same unit (i.e., inch, foot, yard).

subtopics.title: Measure the length of objects and solve problems involving length (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Estimate and measure the length of an object to the nearest inch, foot, yard, centimeter or meter by selecting and using an appropriate tool.
Measure the lengths of two objects using the same unit and determine the difference between their measurements.
Solve one- and two-step real-world measurement problems involving addition and subtraction of lengths given in the same units.

topics.title: Tell time and solve problems involving money

subtopics.title: Tell time and solve problems involving money

outcomes.text: Using analog and digital clocks, express the time in hours and half hours. Explore the concept of a.m. and p.m.
Solve one-step addition and subtraction real-world problems involving either dollar bills within $20 or coins within 20¢. Explore using $ for dollar bills and ¢ symbol for coins.

Using analog and digital clocks, tell and write time to the nearest five minutes using a.m. and p.m. appropriately. Express portions of an hour using the fractional terms half an hour, half past, quarter of an hour, quarter after and quarter til.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems involving either dollar bills within $100 or coins within 100¢ using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately.

topics.title: Understand the place value of three-digit numbers

subtopics.title: Understand the place value of three-digit numbers (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Read and generate numbers from 0 to 100 using standard form and expanded form.
Compose and decompose two-digit numbers using tens and ones. Demonstrate each composition or decomposition with objects, drawings, expressions or equations.
Plot, order and compare whole numbers up to 100.
Round whole numbers from 0 to 100 to the nearest 10 with visual support.

subtopics.title: Understand the place value of three-digit numbers (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Read and write numbers from 0 to 1,000 using standard form, expanded form and word form.
Compose and decompose three-digit numbers in multiple ways using hundreds, tens and ones. Demonstrate each composition or decomposition with objects, drawings and expressions or equations.
Plot, order and compare whole numbers up to 1,000.
Round whole numbers from 0 to 100 to the nearest 10.

topics.title: Add and subtract two- and three-digit whole numbers

subtopics.title: Add and subtract two- and three-digit whole numbers (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Recall addition facts with sums to 10 and related subtraction facts.
Identify the number that is ten more or ten less than a given two-digit number.
Apply a strategy for adding and subtracting a two-digit number (from 11 to 19) and a single digit whole number.
Explore the addition of a two-digit and a single-digit whole number with sums up to 100. Explore the subtraction of a one-digit from a two-digit whole number.

subtopics.title: Add and subtract two- and three-digit whole numbers (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Recall addition facts with sums to 20 and related subtraction facts with automaticity.
Identify the number that is ten more, ten less, one hundred more and one hundred less than a given three-digit number.
Add two whole numbers with sums up to 100 with procedural reliability. Subtract a whole number from a whole number, each no larger than 100, with procedural reliability.
Explore the addition of two whole numbers with sums up to 1,000. Explore the subtraction of a whole number from a whole number, each no larger than 1,000.

topics.title: Solve multiplication and division problems

subtopics.title: Solve multiplication and division problems

outcomes.text: Apply the commutative property of multiplication to find a product of one-digit whole numbers.
Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems within 100.
Solve one-step multiplication and division real-world problems. Multiplication may not exceed two single-digit whole numbers and their related division facts.
Apply the distributive property to multiply a one-digit number and two-digit number. Apply properties of multiplication to find a product of one-digit whole numbers.
Solve one- and two-step real-world problems involving any of four operations with whole numbers.

topics.title: Develop an understanding of equality and multiplication and division

subtopics.title: Develop an understanding of equality and multiplication and division

outcomes.text: Explore division as multiplication with a missing factor using the relationship between multiplication and division.
Determine if multiplication or division equations with no more than three terms are true or false. Multiplication may not exceed two single-digit whole numbers and their related division facts.

Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation, relating three whole numbers, with the product or quotient unknown (e.g., 2 × 5 = __, 10 ÷ 5 = __). Multiplication may not exceed two single-digit whole numbers and their related division facts.
Restate a division problem as a missing factor problem using the relationship between multiplication and division.
Determine and explain whether an equation involving multiplication or division is true or false.
Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation, relating three whole numbers, with the unknown in any position.

topics.title: Identify numerical patterns, including multiplicative patterns

subtopics.title: Identify numerical patterns, including multiplicative patterns

outcomes.text: Determine whether a whole number from 1 to 100 is even or odd.
Explore that a whole number is a multiple of each of its factors. Factors not to exceed single-digit whole numbers.
Extend a numerical pattern when given a one-step addition rule (e.g., when given the pattern 5, 10, 15, use the rule add 5 to extend the pattern)..
Determine and explain whether a whole number from 1 to 1,000 is even or odd.
Determine whether a whole number from 1 to 144 is a multiple of a given one-digit number.
Identify, create and extend numerical patterns.

topics.title: Collect, represent and interpret numerical and categorical data

subtopics.title: Collect, represent and interpret numerical and categorical data (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Sort and represent categorical data (up to four categories) with whole-number values using tables, pictographs or bar graphs. Select appropriate title, labels and units.
Explore representing numerical data with whole-number values using line plots.
Interpret data with whole-number values represented with tables, pictographs or bar graphs to solve one-step “how many more” and “how many less” problems.

Interpret data with whole-number values represented with scaled pictographs or scaled bar graphs. For scaled pictographs, symbols used may only represent quantities of 2, 5 or 10 and only whole symbols may be used. For scaled bar graphs, intervals may only represent quantities of 2, 5 or 10.

subtopics.title: Collect, represent and interpret numerical and categorical data (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Explore interpreting data with whole-number values represented with line plots.
Collect and represent numerical and categorical data with whole-number values using tables, scaled pictographs, scaled bar graphs or line plots. Use appropriate titles, labels and units.
Interpret data with whole-number values represented with tables, scaled pictographs, circle graphs, scaled bar graphs or line plots by solving one- and two-step problems.

topics.title: Understand fractions as numbers and represent fractions

subtopics.title: Understand fractions as numbers and represent fractions

outcomes.text: Explore unit fractions in the form 1/n as the quantity formed by one part when a whole is partitioned into n equal parts. Denominators are limited to 2, 3 and 4.
Explore fractions, less than or equal to a whole, in the form of m/n as the result of adding the unit fraction 1/n to itself m times. Denominators are limited to 2, 3 and 4.
Read and generate fractions, less than or equal to a whole, using standard form.
Represent and interpret unit fractions in the form 1/n as the quantity formed by one part when a whole is partitioned into n equal parts.
Represent and interpret fractions, including fractions greater than one, in the form of m n as the result of adding the unit fraction 1 n to itself m times.
Read and write fractions, including fractions greater than one, using standard form, numeral-word form and word form.

topics.title: Order and compare fractions and identify equivalent fractions

subtopics.title: Order and compare fractions and identify equivalent fractions

outcomes.text: Compare fractional numbers with the same denominator. Denominators are limited to 2, 3 and 4.
Using a visual model, recognize fractions less than a whole that are equivalent to fractions with denominators of 2, 3 or 4 (e.g., 4/8 is equivalent to 1/2).
Plot, order and compare fractional numbers with the same numerator or the same denominator.
Identify equivalent fractions and explain why they are equivalent.

topics.title: Describe and identify relationships between lines and classify quadrilaterals

subtopics.title: Describe and identify relationships between lines and classify quadrilaterals

outcomes.text: Identify points, lines, line segments, perpendicular lines and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
Identify quadrilaterals based on their defining attributes. Quadrilaterals include parallelograms, rhombi, rectangles, squares and trapezoids.
Identify line-symmetric two-dimensional figures.
Describe and draw points, lines, line segments, rays, intersecting lines, perpendicular lines and parallel lines. Identify these in two-dimensional figures.
Identify and draw quadrilaterals based on their defining attributes. Quadrilaterals include parallelograms, rhombi, rectangles, squares and trapezoids.
Draw line(s) of symmetry in a two-dimensional figure and identify line-symmetric two-dimensional figures.

topics.title: Solve problems involving the perimeter and area of rectangles

subtopics.title: Solve problems involving the perimeter and area of rectangles (1 of 2)

outcomes.text: Explore area as an attribute of a two-dimensional figure that can be measured by covering the figure with unit squares without gaps or overlaps.
Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths by counting unit squares. Explore that the area is the same as what would be found by multiplying the side lengths.
Solve mathematical and real-world problems involving the perimeter and area of rectangles with whole-number side lengths using a visual model.
Explore the perimeter and area of composite figures composed of two non-overlapping rectangles with whole-number side lengths.

subtopics.title: Solve problems involving the perimeter and area of rectangles (2 of 2)

outcomes.text: Explore area as an attribute of a two-dimensional figure by covering the figure with unit squares without gaps or overlaps. Find areas of rectangles by counting unit squares.
Find the area of a rectangle with whole-number side lengths using a visual model and a multiplication formula.
Solve mathematical and real-world problems involving the perimeter and area of rectangles with whole-number side lengths using a visual model and a formula.
Solve mathematical and real-world problems involving the perimeter and area of composite figures composed of non-overlapping rectangles with whole-number side lengths.

topics.title: Measure attributes of objects and solve problems involving measurement

subtopics.title: Measure attributes of objects and solve problems involving measurement

outcomes.text: Select and use appropriate tools to measure the length (i.e., inches, feet, yards) of an object.
Explore selecting and using appropriate tools to measure liquid volume (i.e., gallons, quarts, pints, cups) and temperature in degrees Fahrenheit.

Solve one- and two-step addition and subtraction real-world problems within 100 with whole number lengths (i.e., inches, feet, yards), temperatures (i.e., degrees Fahrenheit) or liquid volumes (i.e., gallons, quarts, pints, cups).

Solve one-step multiplication and division real-world problems with whole number lengths (i.e., inches, feet, yards), temperatures (i.e., degrees Fahrenheit) or liquid volumes (i.e., gallons, quarts, pints and cups).
